blocks.c: We sat on the landing of minus three with the sky doing whatever the sky does above eleven floors of impossible basement, and worked it out.
There were two problems and they pulled in opposite directions.

items: The boxes need a hearing. A hearing needs all three of us present and signing. Mrs. Dalisay must come into the building.

The renewal happens at dawn regardless, and at renewal the outgoing caretaker's account settles, and any party present to the renewal is a party to it. If Mrs. Dalisay comes into the building before dawn, she is present at the renewal, and it takes her.

blocks.c: "So she comes after dawn," I said.
"After dawn the boxes are determined by default. There's nothing left to hear." Wen rubbed her eyes. "That's the trap, and it's a good one, and it took a hundred and fifty-one years to build."
"You can't stop a renewal. It's automatic. It's the one thing in the whole document that doesn't need anybody's signature."
I read clause by clause with a torch and a woman who had them memorised, and at 05:20, on page nine, I found the thing.
"Wen. Renewal requires a caretaker in occupation on the premises at the moment of renewal."
"Yes. That's me. That's the whole reason it keeps one."
"But you're the outgoing caretaker. It says the incoming caretaker takes occupation at the moment of renewal, and the outgoing account settles."
"So at the exact moment of renewal," I said slowly, "there has to be somebody in occupation, and it has to be somebody who isn't you."
